newsitem.title: USA: Merrill cuts MCI EPS view.
newsitem.headline: Merrill cuts MCI EPS view.

text.p: Merrill Lynch analyst Dan Reingold said Thursday he cut his earnings projections for MCI Communications Corp for 1997 and 1998 following the company's second quarter results, released on Wednesday.

Reingold said he cut his 1997 year estimate to $1.15 per share from $1.20. He had cut his forecast July 11 from $1.65 a share after MCI warned its results would be hurt by heavy investments it was making to enter U.S. local service markets.
The analyst said he lowered his 1998 year estimate to $1.05 per share from $1.10, after cutting it July 11 from $1.90 per share following the company's announcement.

In published comments, Reingold said the reductions stemmed primarily from his view that trends in the U.S. long distance business -- MCI's core business-- are worsening, and cited an increasingly tougher pricing environment.

He said he lowered his projection for 1998 long distance operating income to $2.55 billion, down $400 million from the forecast he had made following the announcement in November 1996 of MCI's planned merger with British Telecommunications Plc . "In other words, we now expect flat (long distance) operating income (at most two to three percent annual growth) for the three straight years," Reingold wrote.

He added that he continues to believe that pressures are buidling for a renegotiation of the terms of MCI's merger with British Telecom. "We have estimated a compromise of 15 to 25 percent reduction in the exchange value," he said.
If the merger were to fall apart and BT were to revert to holding its 20 percent stake in MCI, MCI shares would likely trade in the $20 range, he said.
MCI stock was up 1/4 at 35-9/16 at mid-afternoon Thursday.
